_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the experimental design.
Both src/gen_prompts.R and src/gen_prompts.py read THIS file, so the R and
Python paths (decision D3) are guaranteed to build identical prompts.
Edit the design here and nowhere else.

rating_labels.3: mixed feelings, neither satisfied nor dissatisfied

_expressiveness_comment: This is the DESIGNED between-topic heterogeneity that makes the random
slopes in the Stan model earn their keep. Reviewers in 'explicit' topics
state their verdict outright, so the rating is easy to read off the text.
Reviewers in 'understated' topics mostly describe, leaving the verdict
implied - so the same embedding geometry carries LESS rating signal.
We therefore KNOW the true slope varies by topic, and can check whether
the hierarchical model recovers that. That is the point of the exercise.

expressiveness.explicit: State your verdict openly and use plainly evaluative language ('I love it', 'total waste of money'). Make your overall opinion unmistakable.
expressiveness.moderate: Mix concrete description of the product with your opinion. State your verdict, but do not dwell on it.
expressiveness.understated: Describe your experience factually and let the verdict remain implied. Avoid overtly evaluative adjectives. Understatement only.

topics.label: a set of printer ink cartridges
a set of cotton bed sheets
a set of stackable storage boxes

system_prompt: You are generating synthetic customer reviews for a statistics teaching dataset. Output ONLY the review text. No preamble, no title, no quotation marks, no markdown, no star rating, and never state the number of stars in digits. Write 40-80 words in plain prose.
user_template: Write a customer review of {product}. The reviewer is {rating_label}. You are {persona}. Say something specific about {aspect}. {expressiveness_instruction}

generation.model_note: Model ID comes from config.R / config.sh, never from this file.

live_slice._comment: What each participant generates live in Block 2 (handover 2.3).

full_corpus._comment: Decision D4 = 50000. 25 topics x 5 ratings x 400 replicates.

_v2_note: v1 produced ~70% EXACT DUPLICATE texts: every replicate in a topic x rating
cell got a byte-identical prompt, and the model collapses to a handful of
completions. Measured: 20 rows per cell, 6 distinct texts.
v2 fixes it two ways, both verified: (a) a per-request `seed` (identical
prompt + varying seed gave 5/5 distinct); (b) a reviewer PERSONA and a review
ASPECT injected per replicate (gave 6/6 distinct, and far more realistic
IMPORTANT: persona and aspect are assigned from the replicate index alone,
using strides coprime with the list lengths, so they are BALANCED across
topic and rating. They are nuisance variation, not confounders - the
designed structure still lives entirely in topic, rating and expressiveness.
